books.section: A. The Ascendancy of the New Right
Reagan, H. W., Clinton, and W. (1980-2001)

stem: Critics argued that Iran-Contra was a constitutional crisis. Which of the following best supports that claim?

options.text: The president's party lost the next presidential election because of the affair
options.misconception: Reagan's vice president, George H. W. Bush, won the 1988 election despite the affair.

options.text: The affair proved that Congress had no role in foreign policy
options.misconception: Congress investigated the affair and held hearings; its role was central, not absent.

options.text: The secret funding denied Congress its power of the purse
The Supreme Court declared the entire Reagan presidency unconstitutional
options.misconception: The Supreme Court never ruled on Iran-Contra, let alone on the presidency itself.

rationales.A: Background: Reagan's vice president, George H. W. Bush, won the 1988 election despite the affair.
rationales.B: Background: Congress investigated the affair and held hearings; its role was central, not absent.
rationales.C: Background: by funding the Contras through secret arms sales, the administration spent money Congress had refused to provide — denying Congress the power of the purse.
rationales.D: Background: the Supreme Court never ruled on Iran-Contra, let alone on the presidency itself.
rationales.general:
1. Ask what makes a scandal a constitutional crisis: not embarrassment, but a broken check.
2. Background: Congress holds the power of the purse — no money may be spent without its approval.
3. Background: by funding the Contras through secret arms sales, the administration spent money Congress had refused to provide.
4. The election was not lost, Congress was not sidelined, and the Court never ruled.
Remember: the crisis was the purse — spending money Congress had said no to.

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of 5 Steps to a 5 2024, Chapter 28, and Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 11. Post-1929 material is paraphrased, not quoted.
stimulus.text: Paraphrase of an account of the Iran-Contra affair: In the mid-1980s, Reagan administration officials secretly sold weapons to Iran, despite an official trade embargo, in order to win Iranian help freeing American hostages held in Lebanon. They then used the money from those sales to aid the Contra rebels fighting Nicaragua's Communist-leaning government, defying limits Congress had placed on aid to the Contras. When the scheme was discovered, Congress held nationally televised hearings.
